data.name: Total balance

data.name: Ad delivery
data.description: Ad platform delivery over time (spend, impressions, clicks) on the unified source language: source scopes by a whop:<campaign>:<group>:<ad> path, exact or with a trailing :* prefix (whop alone or no source = the whole account), and group_by=source groups one path segment deeper than the filter prefix. Only whop:* paths report delivery today; other roots return nothing. breakdown_by=metric returns each delivery measure per bucket plus whole-window data.totals. breakdown_by can instead split delivery by a dimension — age, gender, age_gender, placement, publisher_platform, country, region, device_platform, or impression_device — with the metric parameter picking the measure (spend, impressions, or clicks; defaults to spend). On the placement and publisher_platform dimensions the metric parameter also accepts results, roas, and cost_per_result: conversion-side measures attributed from your own tracked events rather than reported by the ad platform, with results counting conversions that match each ad group's conversion event. Dimension entries don't sum exactly to the totals (the ad platform withholds tiny cells) and are grouped by the ad account's calendar day — they can't re-bucket into time_zone. Spend converts to convert_to (defaults to usd). Whole-account attribution numbers live in the events and people metrics.

data.name: Ad spend
data.description: Total advertising spend across company ad campaigns. Converts to convert_to (defaults to usd) — pass the account's ads reporting currency to match the entity endpoints.

data.name: Events
data.description: Event counts and value sums, filterable and groupable by the unified analytics language. Events are full names (payment.completed, pixel.lead, pixel.page, pixel.custom:<name>). Sources are canonical paths — whop:<campaign>:<group>:<ad>, ext:<platform>:<campaign>:<adset>:<ad>, referrer:<domain>, direct, other — filtered exactly or by trailing :* prefix; a source filter (or attribution_model) makes the query attributed over conversion targets. attribution_model is last_touch (default) or first_touch; under both, a journey with any whop ad touch always attributes to whop (never to an external or referrer source) — the model picks which whop touch credits the entity and which non-whop source wins otherwise. group_by takes one dimension (source, event, country, city, utm_source, hostname, page); attributed queries support source, event, and hostname, where hostname is the credited touchpoint's page. Grouping by source is hierarchical, one path segment deeper than the filter prefix — extra trailing wildcards deepen it (whop:* groups by campaign, whop:*:* by ad group). Requires breakdown_by=metric; entries are "<group>|count" and "<group>|value" (net USD on attributed queries), with per-bucket points and whole-window data.totals. Long-tail group values fold into other past the top 100. Every filter accepts multiple values, matched as OR; a multi-value filter on a dimension other than group_by implicitly breaks entries down by its variants (verbatim, each counted as its own request), composing keys as "<group>|<variant>|measure".

data.name: Payment rule matched volume
data.description: What the payments an account's own rules matched were attempting, in USD. A blocked payment never moved the money, so this is attempted volume rather than revenue. Payments that reached risk assessment without an amount are counted by Payment rule matches but not valued here. Broken down by payment_rule_ids, a payment several rules matched is valued against each of them.

data.name: Payment rule matches
data.description: Payments an account's own payment rules matched, counted once each however many rules matched. Break down by payment_rule_ids for a count per rule, or by action for the split across allow, block, review, and enforce_3ds.

data.name: People
data.description: Unique people (resolved person identities), filterable and groupable by the same unified analytics language as the events metric: full event names, canonical source paths with trailing :* prefixes (a source filter or attribution_model makes the query attributed over conversion targets), and one optional group_by dimension. Uniques only exist at window level, so the response is data.totals only — entries are "<group>|people" (bare "people" without group_by) and never additive across groups or requests. Every filter accepts multiple values, matched as OR; a multi-value filter on a dimension other than group_by implicitly breaks entries down by its variants, same as the events metric.
